sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

2. The petitioner is an accused in connection with C.T. Case No.07 of 2022, pending in the Court of learned Additional District & Sessions Judge, Rayagada, arising out of Andirakancha P.S. Case No.60 of 29.06.2021 for alleged commission of offences under Sections 304-B/498A/306 of IPC read with Section 4 of D.P. Act.
3.

Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned Additional District Judge, Rayagada, by order dated 28.09.2022 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the petitioner is in custody since 27.09.2021 and material witnesses including the uncle of the deceased has already been examined in the meanwhile.
5. It is stated by the learned counsel on instruction that the petitioner is suffering from TB though no material in the said respect is readily available for consideration of this Court.
6. Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail.
7. Taking into account the period of custody and health condition of the petitioner as stated, this Court directs the petitioner to be released on bail.
